findings.detail: NEW HIGH, found while reconciling the 04:30Z alert-commander spawn. The pre-push size-lint gate blocks the fleet on three files, but one of them has ZERO committed contribution to the block. Measured against scripts/audits/size-lint-justification.sh and docs/data/size-lint-baseline.json (threshold 120L, baseline generated 2026-08-22T19:10:16Z, 648 grandfathered entries): the gate fails on growth past a per-file grandfather baseline plus tolerance (+/-10 percent, min 5L), NOT on absolute size. All three offenders are already IN that baseline - pushBctcLayoutHandler.ts baseline 228 actual 252 ceiling 250 (over by 2); tasksMdJanitorJob.ts baseline 906 actual 1012 ceiling 996 (over by 16); ocr_gateway.py baseline 527 actual 594 ceiling 579 (over by 15). ocr_gateway.py is 527L at HEAD - exactly its baseline, a clean PASS. Its entire overage is uncommitted working-tree edit (git diff --numstat 74+/7-, net +67), mtime 2026-08-24 06:40:43 CEST, being written live by dev-pdf-extractor under FIX-OCRGATEWAY-INFLIGHT-BOOKKEEPING-DIVERGES-OS-TRUTH (status IN_PROGRESS). Mechanism verified in source: list_files() is git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard and the check loop counts with wc -l on the working-tree file; nothing references the push range. Consequence: the fleet push is hostage to whatever any agent has dirty at that instant, and splitting the two legitimately-committed files will NOT unblock the push while that P0 edit is open. FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE (tracked P1) is therefore on the critical path of the unblock sprint and outranks the per-file split work - a re-prioritisation call for po, not minted here since the row already exists.

It is a status census, blind to lowercase. The fleet is committing faster than the push block is being resolved. Still gated on the standing PUSH-AUTONOMY-1 user decision; no push attempted by this dispatcher.

Snapshot lookup tally now 3 hits / 4 misses - first hit in three ticks, and it quantifies the mechanism. At 04:30Z the dispatcher wrote cycle-snapshot-04:32.json at 04:32:11Z and the spawned agent read it at approximately 04:32:59Z, reporting it as ~0.8min old: 48 seconds into a 60-second window, i.e. a 12-second margin. The lookup is minute-EXACT, so the hit rate is purely a function of spawn latency against the remainder of the wall-clock minute at write time. This tick wrote at 04:46:37Z leaving only ~23 seconds of that minute, so a miss is the likely outcome. Cost of a miss is a duplicated direct fetch, not wrong data.
